The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> * The RTX A6000 is only available in a handful of zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).  
> * You’ll need a project with billing enabled and the **Compute Engine API** turned on.  
> * Replace placeholders (`<PROJECT_ID>`, `<ZONE>`, `<INSTANCE_NAME>`) with your own values.

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create <INSTANCE_NAME> \
    --project=<PROJECT_ID> \
    --zone=<ZONE> \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Sets the size and performance tier of the boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers). |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script at first boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you prefer a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-16`), just change the `--machine-type` value.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you’re calling the Compute Engine API directly (or via Terraform, Pulumi, etc.), here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "name": "<INSTANCE_NAME>",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Key points

| Field | Explanation |
|-------|-------------|
| `machineType` | Full resource path; choose a type that supports GPUs (e.g., `n1-standard-8`). |
| `guestAccelerators` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `serviceAccounts` | Grants the instance permissions to install drivers, pull images, etc. |
| `metadata.startup-script` | Runs on first boot; here we install the NVIDIA driver (replace with your own script if needed). |

> **Note:** The `acceleratorType` URI must match the zone you’re deploying into. Verify availability via the [GPU Availability page](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#availability).

---

## 3️⃣  Quick Startup Script Example

If you want the instance to automatically install the NVIDIA driver and set up CUDA, create a file named `startup.sh` (used in the gcloud command above):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -eux

# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install prerequisites
apt-get install -y gnupg curl

# Add NVIDIA package repositories
curl -fsSL https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin | tee /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
add-apt-repository "deb http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/ /"

# Install CUDA Toolkit (includes driver)
apt-get update
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers

# Reboot to activate driver
reboot
```

> **Caution:** The script reboots the VM after installing drivers. If you prefer to keep the instance running, remove the `reboot` line and manually reboot later.

---

## 4️⃣  Verify GPU Availability

Before launching, double‑check that the RTX A6000 is available in your chosen zone:

```bash
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(name,zone,available)"
```

If the `available` column shows `0`, pick another zone or wait until capacity frees up.

---

## 5️⃣  Next Steps

1. **Create the instance** using either the CLI or REST call.  
2. **SSH into the VM** once it’s running (`gcloud compute ssh <INSTANCE_NAME>`).  
3. **Verify GPU visibility**:

   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```

   You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

4. **Install any additional software** (CUDA toolkit, cuDNN, PyTorch, TensorFlow, etc.) as required for your workload.

Happy computing! 🚀
